rows: Numerous large tree limbs were ripped off.
Damages were to trees, power lines, awnings and sheds.
Fire department reported Golfball size hail northwest of Ozona.
A thunderstorm downburst overturned a small trailer and blew over a sign.
Large hail stripped leaves off the trees.
A tornado uprooted trees and damaged outbuildings and some mobile homes south of Ozona.
The large hail was reported near mile marker 343 on Interstate 10.
Golfball size hail was reported on State Highway 137.
Golfball size hail was reported on State Highway 163.
Nickel size hail was reported on Highway 163.
Nickel size hail was reported 6 miles south of Ozona on Highway 163.
Half dollar to ping pong size hail was reported along Interstate Highway 10.

A resident in close proximity saw the tornado as it briefly touched down on top of a nearby ridge.
A National Weather Service Cooperative Observer reported large tree limbs down. Several limbs were at least 10 feet long.

The public reported that hail fell until 10 PM, busting windows on two vehicles and a residence. In addition, the large hail killed 12 lambs.
There were 20 power poles blown over and numerous large trees uprooted in Ozona. Also, some homes received minor roof damage. The time of damage was based on radar.
Crockett County Sheriff's Office relayed an estimated 60 mph thunderstorm wind gust reported from the Ozona Volunteer Fire Department about 17 miles west of Ozona along Interstate 10.

A tornado crossed from Val Verde County and tracked north to the Crockett/Val Verde County Line where it dissipated. The tornado damaged power lines.

A person at Twistflower Ranch off of County Road 208 said that hail broke his windshield. He did not have an estimate as to the size of a hail at the time but when he went outside after sunrise, he saw golf ball size hail on the ground.

The Fire Department reported quarter size hail 17 miles south of Ozona.
A NWS employee reported quarter size hail 19 miles south of Ozona.

Public report of ping pong size hail was from mping.
